summary: Ust-Nera Airport (USR/UEMT) is a regional airport serving the remote mining town of Ust-Nera in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), Russian Far East. Situated in one of the most isolated and coldest inhabited regions on Earth, near the famed Pole of Cold at Oymyakon, it primarily supports gold mining operations and connects this far-flung community to regional hubs like Yakutsk. The airport operates under extreme weather conditions, with winter temperatures frequently dropping below -50°C.
faqs:
Q: What is Ust-Nera Airport primarily used for?
A: The airport serves the remote gold mining community of Ust-Nera and provides essential passenger and cargo links to larger Yakutian cities, especially Yakutsk.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Ust-Nera?
A: Summer (June to August) offers the most reliable conditions, as extreme winter cold can sometimes cause flight cancellations or delays.

Q: Are there regular scheduled flights to Ust-Nera?
A: Service is limited and operated primarily by regional carriers such as Polar Airlines, with flights typically routing through Yakutsk.

Q: What is the climate like at Ust-Nera Airport?
A: The airport experiences a subarctic climate with brutally cold winters (often below -50°C) and short, mild summers, conditions that make year-round operations challenging.
transport_tips: There is no public bus or rail service to Ust-Nera, so travelers must arrange a pre-booked taxi or pickup through their hotel or the local mining company in advance. The town is connected only by the R504 Kolyma Highway, so many visitors arrive via small charter aircraft or transfer flights from Yakutsk. Road travel from Yakutsk takes around 18-20 hours and is only feasible during winter on the seasonal ice road.
local_tip: Pack extreme cold-weather gear even in shoulder seasons—layered clothing, insulated boots, and a balaclava are essentials, as waiting on the open tarmac in -40°C or lower is common, and airport facilities offer minimal shelter.
